observed_text: Intensity e-folding length λ/4πk at 450–650 nm, computed from tabulated n and k: Ag 11.6–15.4 nm, Al 6.6–8.3 nm. Reflectance of a continuous film rises smoothly with thickness: half of bulk R at 12–14 nm (Ag) and 4.5–6 nm (Al) at 550 nm. A collective optical response is measured at one atomic layer (graphene, 2.3 % absorption), at 1.65 nm of Ag(111), at 1 nm of seeded Au and in 2 nm particles.
implied_text: No minimum connected buffer is measured. The response scales with how much responding metal the field passes through; λ/4πk (49–65 planes of Ag, 28–36 of Al) is the decay scale of a continuous curve, not a threshold.
description: Reflection has no measured minimum thickness. Reflectance grows continuously with the metal traversed, on the scale of the decay length λ/4πk.
value_text: δ = λ/4πk: Ag 12–15 nm (49–65 planes), Al 6.6–8.3 nm (28–36 planes); a decay length, not a minimum
notes: The first version read 10–20 nm (40–85 planes) as a minimum connected buffer; withdrawn. The key name is kept for stability. value_si is the Ag decay length at 550 nm.

observed_text: Single-layer Fresnel calculation with bulk constants at 550 nm. Free-standing Ag: R = 13.6 % at 5 nm, 38.9 % at 10 nm, 73.8 % at 20 nm, 96.4 % at 50 nm. Al: 41–50 % at 5 nm, 68–74 % at 10 nm. A continuous 5.66 nm Au film matches the same calculation; thinner Au transmits less than the ideal film. Percolation (6–7 nm unseeded Au, 6–12 nm unseeded Ag, 1–3 nm on a copper seed) is abrupt in dc conductance and monotonic in the optical response.
implied_text: Thinning lowers the output continuously because less responding material is traversed. No thickness switches the mirror off; islanding removes dc conduction, not the optical response.
description: Thickness is a crossover: transmitted intensity falls as exp(−d/δ) with δ = λ/4πk, and half of bulk R is a convention.
value_text: half of bulk R at 12–14 nm (Ag), 4.5–6 nm (Al), 550 nm
notes: The first version called this a collapse below 5–10 nm. Morphology is a threshold in dc conductance only (Hövel 2010). value_si is the half-reflectance thickness of free-standing Ag.

observed_text: Plasma periods h/E: 0.28 fs at the measured Al plasmon (15.0 eV); 0.46 fs at the free-electron model value for Ag (9.0 eV); 1.1 fs at the measured Ag plasmon (3.8 eV). A photoemission delay of about 100 as, measured on tungsten, is of the same order.
implied_text: Collective screening and the phase-reversed re-radiation complete on the plasma-period timescale.
description: The electron population responds within a few 10^-16 to 10^-15 s; the image is complete on any macroscopic clock. The data do not separate a faster single-electron step from it.
notes: The first version cited attosecond streaking as a faster single-electron step in these metals; the measurement was on tungsten and is 1e-16 s. value_si lies between the Al and the Ag free-electron periods.

observed_text: Reflectance falls at the plasma or interband edge. Al plasmon 15.0 eV (measured). Ag: bulk R computed from tabulated n and k falls from 95.6 % at 381.5 nm to 5.5 % at 320.4 nm (3.87 eV); the measured plasmon is at 3.8 eV against a free-electron model value of 9 eV.
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock and the reflected beam is lost. In a real metal the edge has a width set by damping and interband transitions; a sharp cutoff belongs to the collisionless model.
description: The same population that reflects below the edge stops reflecting above it. Owned by plasma-frequency-cutoff.
value_text: above the edge: Al 15.0 eV; Ag 3.8–3.9 eV (model 9 eV)
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff, which owns this edge. value_si is the Al plasmon energy over h.

observed_text: Operating window is a drive frequency below the plasma edge (Al) or the interband-screened edge (Ag, 3.8–3.9 eV). No thickness condition is measured: reflectance scales continuously with thickness.
implied_text: This is a driven collective response, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
description: Reflection has an operating condition on drive frequency, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
value_text: ω below the edge (Al 15.0 eV; Ag 3.8–3.9 eV); no thickness condition
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Bulk R computed from tabulated n and k at 450–650 nm: Ag 97.3–99.0 % in the measured sets and 91.9–96.5 % in the fits; Al 90.4–92.4 %. A fresh aluminised mirror measures 90.0–91.4 % at 404–624 nm. No continuous external power to the metal beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Stable phase-reversed reflected beam with material-typical R(λ), at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a macroscopic reflected beam without a hold-power budget.
notes: The reflectance of polished Ag was not read from a mirror measurement. value_si is Ag at 550 nm.

observed_text: No continuous external power is required to maintain the reflected image beyond the incident field itself.
implied_text: Hold-power of the mirror is zero; the drive is the light being reflected.
description: The mirror is not a powered lamp. Continuous draw to hold R is zero.

observed_text: The decay length is δ = λ/4πk (Ag 12–15 nm, Al 6.6–8.3 nm at 450–650 nm), and k is itself an optical constant of the same electrons.
implied_text: QSA takes the measured decay length; it does not derive it from a more primitive node count. It is a decay scale, not a buffer minimum.
description: The decay length is located but not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping lowered from High to Medium on 2026-11-11.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³. KV = 25 kT at 300 K gives V = 2.1–2.4e-26 m³: a sphere 3.4–3.6 nm across or a cube 2.8–2.9 nm on a side. The single-domain diameter is about 200–300 nm.
implied_text: The smallest grain that holds its direction at room temperature on laboratory time is a few nanometres across. Real magnets sit two orders of magnitude above that, so thermal erasure of whole grains is not what limits them. Soft matrices lack the barrier.
description: The thermal-stability size of the latch cell is a few nanometres for Nd2Fe14B. It depends on the waiting time chosen and is not a cliff.
value_text: V ≈ 2.1–2.4e-26 m³ (3.4–3.6 nm sphere); KV = 25 kT
notes: The first version called this volume ~30 nm; a 30 nm cube is about 29 000 kT. 25 kT is the convention for a 100 s measurement. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: A usable motor force is F = ∇(m·B) from a large aligned population. There is no universal millimetre-scale cliff.
implied_text: Macroscopic force is synchronized output of many latched grains. Force scales with aligned moment; the sharp cliff stays at the grain.
description: The sample envelope is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff. No single minimum N for a usable force is extracted.
value_text: force scales with aligned m; no universal N

observed_text: Free-electron gyromagnetic ratio γe/2π = 28 024.951 MHz/T (CODATA 2022).
implied_text: Baseline single-spin clock of the latch. Write/erase of a hard magnet is set by field sweep and wall motion, not this carrier.
description: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession clock; holding the state does not require running that clock as a power draw.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B anisotropy K1 = 4.3–4.9 MJ/m³ at room temperature (4.30 on single crystals, 4.9 in another tabulation); per-grain barrier ΔE ≈ K1V. A real magnet reverses at 16–18 % of the anisotropy field. Holding costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Anisotropy holds the grain's moment along an axis. Exchange, a separate resource, makes the grain one moment. Energy is spent only on write/erase.
description: The latch exists because a barrier protects orientation at zero hold-power.
notes: Barrier energy is K1V, not K1 alone. The first version used 4.5 MJ/m³, which is inside the range but was not found in an opened source. value_si is mid-range.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B Curie temperature 585–588 K; commercial grades list 310–380 °C. Iron has a hundredth of the anisotropy and a Curie temperature of 1043 K.
implied_text: Loss of exchange order at Tc removes the moment itself. The Curie temperature is set by exchange, not by kT exceeding the anisotropy barrier.
description: Thermal loss of magnetic order at the Curie point, an exchange threshold.
notes: The first version attributed this collapse to the anisotropy barrier.

observed_text: τ = τ0 exp(KV/kT). KV = 25 kT (100 s with τ0 = 1e-9 s) at 300 K is a 3.4–3.6 nm sphere for Nd2Fe14B.
implied_text: Same barrier, smaller volume: the retention time falls exponentially. There is no critical size.
description: Small grains lose their direction thermally without reaching Tc; the size quoted depends on the waiting time.
value_text: KV ≈ 25 kT (≈3.5 nm sphere, Nd2Fe14B, 100 s)
notes: Primary owner of this crossover is superparamagnetism. The comparison with a thin-film mirror in the first version is withdrawn.

observed_text: A transverse shock of 22.3 GPa turns Nd2Fe14B into a weak magnet; 6.26–7.16 GPa demagnetizes sintered magnets by intergranular fracture, recoverable by annealing. Hydrogen decrepitation gives a demagnetized hydrided powder.
implied_text: Shock and chemical breakdown remove remanence without reaching Tc, through fracture, a pressure-induced change of magnetic phase, or a change of material.
description: Shock and hydrogen decrepitation erase a hard magnet below its Curie point.
notes: Two measured shock points, no threshold established. No source was found for plastic deformation, which the first version listed.

observed_text: A static magnet at rest produces no continuous I²R or hysteresis heat.
implied_text: Stable directional moment and static field/force at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / KV / lattice envelope.
description: Holding the latched state costs zero watts. Energy is the write/erase loop area only.

observed_text: The first sintered magnet had coercivity 960 kA/m (about 1.2 T), 16–18 % of the 6.7–7.65 T anisotropy field. In simulation a defect-free cubic grain reaches 3.94 T against an ideal 6.09 T, about 65 %.
implied_text: QSA does not have a buffer/barrier specification for the mesoscale write threshold (nucleation, grain boundaries, dipolar coupling).
description: Coercivity is a mesoscale quantity the mapping does not specify. With the stability size two orders below the single-domain size, this step, not KV, limits a real magnet.

observed_text: One electron at a surface is one conversion. Intensity sets the number of electrons and not their maximum energy. No collection depth was sourced.
implied_text: No collective buffer is specified. One electron at a surface is the hardware.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle.
notes: How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.

observed_text: Photoelectrons from core states of tungsten emerge about 100 attoseconds after those from the conduction band. This is a relative delay between two channels; no absolute latency was sourced.
implied_text: The conversion is finished on any optical-cycle-averaged laboratory clock.
description: Measured relative emission delays are about 100 attoseconds.

observed_text: Polycrystalline work functions: Cs 1.95, K 2.29, Al 4.25, Ag 4.33, W 4.55, Cu 4.55, Pt 5.41 eV. Kmax = hν − φ above threshold.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Below it (linear regime) conversion does not occur. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
description: The photoelectric effect is a single-particle energy gate at the work function.
notes: value_si is tungsten, 4.55 eV, in joules.

observed_text: hν < φ: no one-photon emission at zero temperature. Above φ the yield rises from zero as (hν − φ)², so there is an onset and no step. The gate is rounded on the scale of kT, 25.85 meV at 300 K (0.57 % of 4.55 eV).
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. The collapse is an energy threshold rounded by temperature.
description: Below the work function the gate stays shut.
notes: value_si is tungsten. A patchy surface spreads the observed onset over tenths of an eV (W(100) 4.65 eV against 4.55 eV polycrystalline): a crossover on top of the threshold.

observed_text: A surface-specific φ, a photocurrent that starts there with a quadratic onset, and a linear Kmax(ν) above it.
implied_text: The stable output is the threshold itself plus the above-threshold kinetic-energy line.
description: The machine’s stable product is a work-function gate and a linear surplus-energy line.

observed_text: QSA takes measured φ. Crystal faces differ (W(100) 4.65 eV against 4.55 eV polycrystalline).
implied_text: No derivation of the 2–5 eV range from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: Do not identify φ with silver's optical edge: reflectance minimum 3.92 eV against φ 4.33 eV.
